Strelka2 2.9.10: strelka2, GetChromDepth, MergeRunStats, and HTSlib's bgzip, tabix and htsfile, bgzf_cat – the
programs of Strelka's somatic workflow
Licence: GNU GPL version 3 or later (LICENSE.txt, COPYRIGHT.txt in this folder). It contains a subset of Boost 1.58
(LICENSE.boost), HTSlib 1.7-6-g6d2bfb7 (LICENSE.htslib), CodeMin 1.0.5 (LICENSE.codemin), RapidJSON 1.1.0
(LICENSE.rapidjson) and bgzf_extras 0.1 (LICENSE.bgzf-extras), and is built with zlib 1.3.1 (LICENSE.zlib); the loader
is Emscripten's runtime (MIT and NCSA: LICENSE.emscripten). samtools 1.6 (LICENSE.samtools) and pyflow 1.1.20
(COPYRIGHT.pyflow) are part of the upstream release, used by its own workflow scripts. THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt
lists them. config/ holds Strelka's empirical variant scoring models, as released.
Upstream source: https://github.com/Illumina/strelka (release 2.9.10, commit 1c8f1be330dc6f58568c82468a9da1c5f32fb54a):
strelka-2.9.10.release_src.tar.bz2 – in ../../../licenses/sources/.

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm,
commit bfacba3): Emscripten 3.1.64, one thread. The modules are used here as that project built them: the page runs
each command in a worker of its own (assets/js/threads-worker.mjs). Everything needed to build them again is described
in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/.

Changes to the source (tools/strelka2/browser.patch, htslib.patch and rapidjson.patch there): an assignment operator
of RapidJSON that cannot be used is deleted; Strelka's run-statistics counters are 64-bit numbers on 32-bit
WebAssembly too; bgzip stops (status 2) when asked for more than one thread. Calling, scoring and the models are
unchanged.
Strelka's workflow is a set of Python 2 scripts (pyflow). strelka2-somatic.mjs, from genomics-wasm's runtime/
(GNU GPL 3 or later, unchanged), is their translation for the somatic workflow: it runs the programs above one after
another, with upstream's commands, segments and file handling; index.mjs is the workbench's small part of it (the
paths of the terminal). In the workbench's terminal configureStrelkaSomaticWorkflow.py checks the input with the
messages of upstream's configure script and writes RUNDIR/runWorkflow.py, which runs the workflow (assets/js/somatic.js).
Only the somatic workflow is here; -m local only, and the tasks run one after another.

Checked against Strelka2 2.9.10 built natively from the same release, run by its own Python 2 workflow
(genomics-wasm's comparison: 13 of 13 cases with the HCC1395 tumour/normal reads – exome mode, call regions, callable
regions, EVS features, configuration files, single regions; and in the workbench with the example data): the same
VCF records and index queries, and the same run statistics (but for the times).
